recommendation: Keep the source fix. It is a narrow restoration of the approved FHIR-42834 clarification and preserves the later FHIR-48702 URL-encoding structure.
issue_request: FHIR-42834 was Applied/Persuasive for FHIR-core search. It asked to clarify the Escaping Search Parameters examples because a query with a backslash-escaped comma changes the comma from an OR delimiter into a literal character in the search value.
initial_application: Historical source commits badb98fe3e2df7a0e5c8bb10364697439ac3655b and 7a31ece31b504b076d7257877184ae3a8047d7a1 applied FHIR-42834 to source/search.html by replacing the escaped-comma same-meaning example and adding a separate example that explains escaped and non-escaped delimiters in the same request.
additional_context: A later Applied issue, FHIR-48702, refactored source/search.html to add URL-encoding guidance and readable unencoded examples. Its implementation commit d83729a5d4743f1218b4e53aad9e70c5363880da accidentally reintroduced the backslash-escaped comma form into the same-meaning list. FHIR-48702 is already represented on the combined branch, so no duplicate related decision was published.
reconciliation: Changed source/search.html so the same-meaning list uses a mixed percent-encoded comma example, while leaving the following escaped-delimiter paragraph as the place that demonstrates the different two-value semantics of a backslash-escaped comma.
source_changes: source/search.html:2708 now uses http://acme.org/fhir/ValueSet/123%2Chttp://acme.org/fhir/ValueSet/124,ValueSet/125 in the same-meaning percent-encoding list instead of the backslash-escaped comma form.

related_jiras.note: Later URL-encoding cleanup refactored the same search.html section and reintroduced the escaped-comma form into the same-meaning list; it is already represented on the combined branch.

evidence_items.summary: Applied/Persuasive FHIR-I issue asking to clarify search escaping examples where an escaped comma was incorrectly shown as same-meaning.
evidence_items.learned: The final decision establishes that the escaped-comma form must be separated from percent-encoding examples because it changes the search value semantics.

evidence_items.summary: The reporter explained that backslash-escaping the comma makes it part of the search value, and Gino Canessa replied that the spec text was a typo needing a Jira ticket.
evidence_items.learned: The discussion confirms the semantic bug addressed by the source edit.
